findings.title: Removing the BuildIndex-wide lock allows concurrent duplicate index builds for the same key
findings.body: BuildIndex previously held `b.cacheMu` for the whole function, which serialized builds and guaranteed that only one index per NamespacedResource was ever constructed. Now the lock is only taken around the final `b.cache[key] = idx` write. Nothing prevents two goroutines from calling BuildIndex for the same key concurrently (e.g. `searchSupport.getOrCreateIndex` does an unsynchronized GetIndex-then-build, and it is reachable from both the watch-event handler and concurrent Search calls). Consequences: (1) for file-backed indexes both goroutines call `bleve.New(dir, ...)` on the same directory, so the second call fails with a 'path already exists' error and the request errors out; (2) duplicated full index builds waste CPU/IO; (3) the loser's bleve index is overwritten in the cache and never closed, leaking file handles/memory. If the goal is finer-grained locking, a per-key lock (or singleflight) is needed rather than no mutual exclusion at all.

findings.title: TotalDocs iterates b.cache without holding cacheMu
findings.body: `TotalDocs` ranges over `b.cache` with no lock while `BuildIndex` now writes to that map under `b.cacheMu` from arbitrary goroutines (index builds triggered by watch events or search requests). Concurrent map read and map write is a fatal, unrecoverable Go runtime error ('concurrent map read and map write') that crashes the process. Previously this was partially masked because BuildIndex held the write lock for its whole duration; with the finer locking, writes happen far more often and at unpredictable times. TotalDocs should take `b.cacheMu.RLock()`.

findings.title: errgroup goroutines share the outer `err` and `totalBatchesIndexed` variables (data race, lost errors)
findings.body: Inside `group.Go(...)` the code does `_, _, err = s.build(...)` assigning to the `err` declared in the enclosing function, and increments the shared `totalBatchesIndexed`. With `initWorkers > 1` these are concurrent unsynchronized writes: a genuine data race (will be flagged by `-race`) and, worse, one goroutine's error can be clobbered by another goroutine before `group.Wait()` returns, and `err = group.Wait()` can be overwritten by a still-running assignment. Since this function now runs at server construction and its error aborts startup, misreporting matters. Use a local `err :=` inside the closure and an atomic counter.

findings.title: Init failure in NewResourceServer leaks the server context and background goroutines
findings.body: `NewResourceServer` creates `ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(...)` and stores `cancel` on the server. When `s.Init(ctx)` fails, the function returns `nil, err` without calling `cancel()`. Anything already started during Init — the storage backend's watch poller started by `searchSupport.init` via `WatchWriteEvents`, and the broadcaster/watcher if `initWatcher` partially succeeded — keeps running against a context that is never cancelled, leaking goroutines, DB connections and the context itself for the lifetime of the process. Call `cancel()` (or `s.Stop`) on the error path.

findings.title: Removing per-request Init() checks means requests are still served after Stop()
findings.body: `Stop` communicates shutdown by setting `s.initErr = "service is stopping"` / `"service is stopped"`, and the only thing that ever read `initErr` on the request path were the `if err := s.Init(ctx); err != nil` guards that this PR deleted from Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/History/Origin/IsHealthy/PutBlob/GetBlob. After this change, requests arriving after `Stop()` no longer fail fast; they fall through to a backend whose context has been cancelled, producing confusing 'context canceled' errors (or, for blob/diagnostics paths, operating on torn-down state) instead of the intended shutdown error. Either keep a cheap state check at the entry of the handlers or drop the now-dead `initErr` shutdown signalling in `Stop`.

findings.title: Index build now runs synchronously in the constructor with an uncancellable, unbounded context
findings.body: `s.Init(ctx)` is invoked from `NewResourceServer` with a `context.Background()`-derived context that has no deadline, and it performs the full search index build (`searchSupport.init`, which lists every resource of every namespace). Constructing the resource server therefore blocks Grafana/storage-server startup for as long as indexing takes, with no timeout and no way for the caller to cancel; a slow or unresponsive database makes startup hang indefinitely rather than failing or degrading. Consider a bounded context or kicking the index build off asynchronously while keeping the lifecycle/backend init synchronous.

findings.title: Storage-server integration test now skipped for postgres, leaving only mysql coverage
findings.body: With sqlite3 already skipped, adding an unconditional skip for postgres means `TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer` only ever runs against mysql in CI. Given this PR changes resource-server startup to initialize unified storage (including index building) inside `NewResourceServer`, the postgres startup path is exactly what this test would have covered. The TODO has no tracking issue; at minimum reference one so the coverage gap is not forgotten.
